findings.description: `save(p)` starts an individual share or download without consulting Save all’s in-progress state, while `tap()` uses a snapshot and does not recheck `handed` before each download. If someone taps a photo during a download batch, that photo can download immediately and again when the batch reaches it; an individual share pending before Save all can likewise put the same file in both share attempts.
findings.title: A photo can be saved twice during a batch

evidence.explanation: The individual path writes `handed` only after sharing resolves or its download starts, without checking Save all’s `busy` state. Save all snapshots eligible files before its share or spaced download loop and does not recheck each photo after waiting.

Chrome provides a site permission specifically for automatic downloads.

evidence.explanation: The download loop in `web/saveall.js` records a photo in `handed` immediately after calling `download()`, while `downloadFile` in `web/index.html` creates and clicks an anchor without confirming that the browser accepted or saved the file. Because subsequent Save all batches exclude recorded photos, a download blocked by automatic-download permissions can be counted as saved and omitted from future attempts.

findings.description: `tap()` displays `Saved ${ready.length}` before trying any download and catches each thrown download error with only a console warning. If URL creation or a download-start call throws, the affected photo remains eligible for retry, but the person receives a success message rather than notice that it failed.
findings.title: Failed downloads still show as saved

evidence.explanation: The toast runs before the loop, while the catch only logs a warning and never corrects that message; the page passes `downloadFile`, whose URL creation or click can throw, as the download callback.

findings.description: `saveBatch()` counts still-arriving photos solely from `incoming`, but the transfer handler removes an entry before `done()` finishes asynchronous hash verification and puts its file in `files`. A Save all tap during that interval reports “Nothing new to save” when the completed photo is neither counted as arriving nor ready.
findings.title: Verifying photos appear missing

evidence.explanation: The last-chunk handler deletes `incoming` before calling `done`; `done` awaits hashing before setting `files`. The new batch calculation reads only those two maps.
